items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: In fact, he was there I think before George Shearing. Shearing came in a little bit after Erroll had split. But he was beautiful to play with and listen to.

ctx.x: On 52nd Street, yeah. We used to play there all the time. In fact, he was there I think before George Shearing. Shearing came in a little bit after Erroll had split. But he was beautiful to play with and listen to.

He had 52nd Street swinging! I mean, everybody would run from one joint to the other to hear the sets on time, so that nine times out of ten you could hear who you wanted to after you got through listening to any particular artist that was down there. You'd just go in the next club and have a drink and so forth, and see who plays next. And that's the way we used to do it then. I used to go down and hear Diz, and I'd say "Oh yeah, mmm-hmm," and see what he's playing and see what he's thinking about as far as his…
